text:
Alexis Lafreniere has 22 points in 21 games, 10 of them goals, and The Hockey Writers is calling it a step up. At 25, the 2020 first overall pick is playing like a first-line winger, scoring at 3.39 points per 60, well above last season's 2.37.

How much of it holds? Some of the goals are running hot: 10 on 7.5 expected, shooting 22% against 15% last season. The chances themselves are better too, 1.15 expected goals per 60 on his own shots against 0.94 a year ago, which is the real progress. With him on the ice at five on five, the Rangers take 55% of the expected goals, and they've been a little unlucky to score as few as they have. Our talent range has him around 70 points for the season.

He's always been more than a shooter. Evolving-Hockey had him 29th among forwards in wins above replacement last season, with 93rd-percentile defensive impact against tough competition, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found 57% of his shots come off the rush. Watch him in the first seconds after the Rangers win the puck back. That's when he's at his best.
